thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate from hosted-runtime (kv-cache OOM) in us-west-2. 5xx spike + 20% latency increase across generation endpoints. Alert group: kv-cache/continuous-batching. Root keys: long prompt contexts.

samir: I'm on it, paging into Zoom. seeing repeated `kv_cache::alloc failed` in logs. pushing logs to #eng-runtime.

jordan: support-bot flagged 3 customers with >500 errors in last 10m (customer-42, analytics-pro, chatty-app). CS is already reaching out.

leo: snippets from runtime:```
[2025-03-11T17:50:12Z] kv_cache alloc failed: requested 2378234880 bytes > available 2147483648
[2025-03-11T17:50:12Z] continuous_batcher: inflight_prefix_len=185000 total_kv_size=2.2GB
```

maya_k: ok hypothesis = runaway context windows hitting kv-cache size limits + continuous batching merging very long prefixes. can we short-circuit batching or evict long entries?

samir: immediate mitigation: disable continuous batching flag on hosted runtime and set eviction threshold for single KV entry > 4MB. preparing hotfix.

leo: how to flip config? I can patch the feature-flag service. command: `PATCH /api/flags/continuous_batching {"enabled":false}`. also set `kv.max_entry_bytes=4194304`.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: flag-change v2 -> canary (10%). CI checks pass. rolling canary to 3 nodes in us-west-2.

samir: canary looks good so far, no regressions on stable traffic samples. error rate down ~60% in canary shards. promoting to 50%.

opsbot: note: disabling batching increases per-token CPU but avoids OOM. watch latency.

jordan: CS update: customers impacted slowed down, most errors are 503s not incorrect outputs. opened incident page and notified enterprise contacts.

maya_k: additionally set a temporary prompt-length validation: reject requests with context_bytes > 5MB with 400 + friendly message. we'll backfill a migration path for customers.

leo: pushed validation to edge gateway: `if (context_size > 5_000_000) return 400 "context too large"`. live in edge-canary.

support-bot: queued outbound messages to affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full fix.

samir: rolling out full flag change to us-west-2. monitoring.

deploy-bot: flag-change v2 - rollout 100% in us-west-2 complete.

maya_k: metrics: 5xx down to baseline in 12m after full rollout, latency +8% p95 (expected). KV cache memory usage dropped from 92%->48% on avg.

leo: follow-ups: (1) implement LRU eviction by total prefix bytes, (2) add guardrail for continuous-batcher to refuse merging prefixes when single request > 128k tokens, (3) telemetry to capture top-100 largest contexts per day. I'll open tickets.

samir: handing off to @maya_k for post-incident ops and RCA. I'll be offline for dinner but reachable.

maya_k: taking over. timeline and action items posted to incident doc (link: https://internal.redwood/incident/2025-03-11-kv-cache-oom). owners assigned.

jordan: postmortem requested, severity P1 for business impact, SOC/Legal looped since enterprise customers were affected.

opsbot: automated checklist: create rollback plan, capture heap dump from affected nodes, export KV key-size histogram.

samir: quick note: we saw one request with a concatenated transcript that was 1.8M tokens -> caused multi-GB KV entry. we need better client-side limits and explicit guidance in docs.

maya_k: agreed. action: add client SDK validation and docs update. also schedule load test with synthetic long-contexts.

support-bot: incident status updated -> mitigated. CS will follow up with impacted customers with summary and remediation timeline.

leo: adding retro item: consider adaptive batching heuristics (batch by token-count not request-count) to avoid merging long contexts.

maya_k: closing incident thread in 2h after RCA draft. thanks everyone for quick response. :heart:
